column3: The Hebrew explicitly repeats my voice to God and presents His heeding as completed.
The Hebrew has a singular hand; BSB uses hands.
The Hebrew names God as the object remembered, not an address You, O God.
The Hebrew names the watchings of his eyes and does not explicitly say too troubled to speak.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says with my heart rather than in it.
The Hebrew leaves the rejected object unnamed; BSB supplies us.
The Hebrew names a word rather than explicitly a promise.
The Hebrew makes God the subject shutting compassion in anger; BSB makes His anger the subject.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has Your wonder in the singular; BSB has wonders.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says in holiness or the sanctuary without explicitly saying our God.
The Hebrew presents making His strength known as completed; BSB uses display.
The Hebrew names an arm rather than power.
The Hebrew describes trembling rather than swirling.
The Hebrew pictures the skies giving a voice; BSB specifies thunder.
The Hebrew directly names the voice of Your thunder without an explicit verb of resounding.
The Hebrew says the footprints were not known; BSB says not to be found.
Close to the Hebrew.
